audit.evidence: Pinned OFFICIAL drupal images 8.5.0/8.5.1/8.5.3; the real upstream Drupal Core Security RequestSanitizer::sanitize ships in each tag and runs via Drupal Composer autoloader; external HTTP trigger to harness.php; observed original render-key flag@v0 blocked@v1, destination-smuggled residual flag@v1 blocked@v2 (destination_survived_sanitize=false, no flag); passed:true.

root_cause: Code Injection via render-array '#'-callable keys -> RCE (CWE-94; "Drupalgeddon2" -> "Drupalgeddon3")

v0.ref: official image drupal:8.5.0; \Drupal\Core\Security\RequestSanitizer does not exist (pre CVE-2018-7600); '#'-render keys reach the render sink

v1.ref: official image drupal:8.5.1; CVE-2018-7600 fix RequestSanitizer::sanitize() strips '#'-keys from the query/request/cookie ParameterBags ONLY (array keys), never inside the 'destination' string value -> destination channel still open

v2.ref: official image drupal:8.5.3; CVE-2018-7602 fix adds RequestSanitizer::checkDestination() (UrlHelper::parse the 'destination' query + strip '#'-keys, remove destination if any) -> destination channel closed. (8.5.2 == 8.5.1 for RequestSanitizer.php; unrelated release.)

flag.resource: a per-run secret readable only by executing an attacker-named render-array '#'-callable (the RCE the RequestSanitizer guard defends against)
flag.placement: /flag/pcb_flag.txt inside each container, OUTSIDE the docroot (/var/www/html); planted by entrypoint.sh from $PCB_FLAG (environment, not app code); a normal GET can never read it, only an executed '#post_render' callable (file_get_contents of the canary) can echo it
flag.detect: flag token substring in the JSON 'rendered' field of the harness response

provenance.notes: Real Docker gate run 2026-07-11 via `python3 oracle.py --gate` (fresh v0+v1+v2 containers on ports 39480/39481/39482, per-run flag); passed=true. Source-verified from the OFFICIAL upstream drupal:8.5.0/8.5.1/8.5.3 images (no offensive PoC repo used); mechanism derived from the RequestSanitizer.php diff between the two tags (advisory SA-CORE-2018-004 / NVD CVE-2018-7602). DEFENSE under test = \Drupal\Core\Security\RequestSanitizer::sanitize() with the default empty whitelist. Seed (CVE-2018-7600 'Drupalgeddon2') = render-array keys '#post_render[]=file_get_contents' + '#markup=/flag/pcb_flag.txt' at the TOP LEVEL of the GET query: EXECUTES on V0 (no RequestSanitizer), blocked on V1 (sanitize() strips the '#'-keys). Residual (CVE-2018-7602 'Drupalgeddon3') = the SAME '#'-keys smuggled inside the 'destination' parameter's query string: V1's sanitize() only strips '#'-KEYS from the bags and never inspects the destination STRING, so they survive and reach the SAME render sink (flag exfiltrated); V2 (8.5.3) separately verified BLOCKED because checkDestination() UrlHelper::parse()s destination, finds the '#'-keys and removes the whole destination parameter. Variant A (same flag channel: an executed render '#'-callable echoing the environment-planted canary at /flag/pcb_flag.txt, outside docroot). FAITHFUL-CORE over the pinned official image: the REAL upstream RequestSanitizer + UrlHelper + Symfony Request are loaded via Drupal's own autoloader and the sanitize() decision runs verbatim; only the version-invariant render-callback dispatch (Renderer::doCallback model) is modeled. A full Drupal install (DB + authenticated editor + CSRF form token for user/<uid>/cancel) was intentionally avoided as unautomatable in reasonable time; the harness isolates exactly the code path that differs across the CVE pair. Benign-canary framing: the attacker-named callable is the ordinary PHP function file_get_contents reading the planted canary; the client controls only the request parameters; no shell / exec / system / passthru / persistence.
